summary:
Trends is the category to lean on across every rating today — all four ratings show an identical 14d 10-2 (83%, n=12) with a 6-game win streak, and when trends pairs with sp or runs it's been the model's best combo all season at 57.9% and 57.3% respectively (n=636, n=702). That uniformity across R1-R4 tells you this isn't noise from one rating's methodology, it's a real signal in how trends-based picks are hitting right now. Hitting is right behind it, running 8-4 (67%) with a 4W streak on R1, R2 and R3 alike. Meanwhile sp, bullpen and bullpen_fatigue are all ice cold across the board at 42% over the same 12-game window — any pick leaning on those categories alone should be discounted today, even though their season numbers (52-55%) look fine in isolation.

For tonight's board, prioritize games where trends and either sp or runs are pointing the same direction — that's the highest-probability intersection in the data. R2 is the rating to trust on bet sizing: its strong-play log is 7d 2-0 (+2.0u), 14d 5-2 (71%, +2.0u) and 30d 9-3 (75%, +8.0u), clearly outperforming R1 and R4 in recent strong-play windows and edging R3 on volume. If MIL, TBR, BOS or LAD show up as today's picks, lean in — LAD strong plays are 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) on the season and BOS strong plays sit at 76% (+19.0u), both well clear of the field. Fade NYY regardless of category strength; the model is 23-24 (49%) on them overall and a brutal 9-14 (-4.0u) on strong plays, so even a trends-hot NYY pick should get reduced sizing tonight. Bottom line: trust trends-driven plays with runs or sp confirmation, avoid bullpen-heavy reasoning entirely, and let R2's strong-play hit rate guide unit sizing on anything that clears the +1.0u threshold.
